links.outcome: Sensitivity/specificity of AI-human double reading versus human-human double reading, plus human reads per image
links.effect: DR/RVO: no significant difference (all p≥0.05). AMD: sensitivity 0.916 and 0.950 (p<0.001) vs 0.845, one combination 0.842 (p=0.742); human reads 1.02-1.11 vs 2.00-2.10 per image.
links.quote: Across AI-human combinations, sensitivity and specificity did not differ significantly from human-human reading (all p ≥ 0.05; specificity differences ≤0.001).

links.outcome: AI-human double reading compared with conventional human-human double reading on the same images
links.effect: Comparable accuracy for DR and RVO with about 46-49% fewer human reads; AMD sensitivity higher in two of three configurations, with lower specificity (≥0.978).
links.quote: Accordingly, human–human double reading required 2.00 to 2.10 human reads per image, whereas AI–human double reading required 1.02 to 1.11, corresponding to a 46% to 49% reduction in human reading events ( Table 2 ).

links.outcome: Standalone AI sensitivity versus prespecified 0.99 target on local single-center cohort
links.effect: Standalone sensitivity 0.929 for AMD and 0.931 for DR, below the 0.99 target; 0.994 for RVO. Attributed partly to domain shift.
links.quote: A related consideration is that, as a standalone classifier, the AI system did not reach its prespecified operating target of 0.99 sensitivity for two of the three diseases, achieving a standalone sensitivity of 0.929 for AMD and 0.931 for DR, although it reached 0.994 for RVO.

links.outcome: Effect of AI operating threshold (target sensitivity 0.95 vs 0.995) on workflow sensitivity, specificity, and reads
links.effect: For AMD, raising target sensitivity from 0.95 to 0.995 raised workflow sensitivity from 0.854 to 0.940 (AI-R1-R2), lowered specificity from 0.992 to 0.967, and increased reads from 1.04-1.07 to 1.10-1.17.
links.quote: For AMD, raising the AI target sensitivity from 0.95 to 0.995 increased workflow sensitivity from 0.854 to 0.940 for AI–R1–R2 and from 0.921 to 0.973 for AI–R1–R3, while workflow specificity fell from 0.992 to 0.967 and from 0.991 to 0.966 respectively, and mean human reads per image rose from 1.04–1.07 to 1.10–1.17.

links.quote: AI–human double reading with arbitration substantially reduced repeated human reading while preserving diagnostic reliability for DR and RVO and demonstrating reader-configuration-dependent performance for AMD.

links.quote: Although standalone AI specificity was as low as 0.925 for RVO and 0.938 for AMD, workflow specificity remained 0.978 or higher across all diseases.

links.effect: False-negative correction: AMD 2–20/67 (3–30%); DR 17–20/37 (46–54%); RVO 0–1/2, despite human review/arbitration.
links.quote: Correction of standalone AI false negatives was less consistent (AMD, 2–20 of 67 [3–30%]; DR, 17–20 of 37 [46–54%]; RVO, 0–1 of 2) ( Table S3 ).
